text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: inference-service-rrg (prod, az1a) p99 latency spike > 2s for 3m, error-rate 5% (auto-detected). Link: https://monitoring.example/alert/AR-1932

tanya_sre: acked. I'm oncall. gathering quick context.

mike_infra: seeing a coincident kernel patch rollout in az1a nodes 3h ago in the node pool. Could be NIC offload interaction.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-06-21T02:12:23 UTC: kernel/5.12.16 -> 5.12.18 rolled to pool-az1a-group-6 (batch: 20 nodes).

sam_product: customers noticing chat completions timing out. Any known customer-facing errors?

maria_support: two customers reported 504s and high latency in EU region routing through az1a. Support ticket IDs: #8472, #8481.

leo_runtime: quick telemetry: kv-cache-hit rates unchanged, token throughput drops on requests routed to az1a. Suggesting network egress issue rather than model stall.

tanya_sre: can we validate packet drop / NIC stats on a sample host? mike, can you run ethtool + dmesg?

mike_infra: running quick checks...

mike_infra: ```
# on host ip-10-1-4-22
sudo ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
  rx-checksumming: on
  tx-checksumming: on
  scatter-gather: on
  tcp-segmentation-offload: off
  tcp6-gso-offload: off
  gso: on
  gro: on
  lro: off

# dmesg | tail
[ 12345.678901] igb 0000:03:00.0 eth0: detected TX hangs, resetting
[ 12346.678902] igb_something NIC watchdog: tx_hang
```

mike_infra: iperf between node and gateway shows intermittent bursts of packet loss ~1-2% and retransmits during high qps.

leo_runtime: that aligns with the increase in tail latency for streaming tokens. KV cache and batching are sensitive to packet loss on control plane and model shard traffic.

sam_product: what's the blast radius? % of inference requests impacted and which customers?

maria_support: preliminary: ~8% of prod inference requests were routed to az1a in the last 10m, and of those ~40% experienced >1s added latency or 5xx. Customers on EU region with strict routing saw impact.

leo_runtime: mitigation options: 1) Reroute new requests away from az1a (fast) 2) Mark az1a nodes unhealthy at LB / router level (drain) 3) Roll back kernel/patch in pool (slower, disruptive) 4) Live-config change to increase cross-AZ capacity + prefer warm cold pools.

ben_oncall: if we can reroute within the control plane quickly that's least risky. How do we flip routing?

leo_runtime: can flip routing weights in the router config. Example call (internal):

```
POST /v1/routing/update
{
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "prefer_zones": ["az1b","az1c"],
  "exclude_zones": ["az1a"],
  "drain_ttl": 300
}
```

I can push this if SRE approves. It will divert new requests; existing sticky sessions may still go to az1a for a minute or so.

tanya_sre: approve. Push it and monitor. Also start a node drain + autoscaler config to avoid scheduling in az1a until root cause fixed.

leo_runtime: pushing now... :gear:

leo_runtime: router response: 200 OK. routing weights updated. New requests should avoid az1a within ~10-20s.

mike_infra: initiating cordon/drain in pool-az1a-group-6 for the nodes with tx_hang evidence. running `kubectl cordon; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` now.

maria_support: notifying affected customers: we will update status page and follow-up with mitigation timeline.

status-bot: <status page draft> "We are investigating elevated latency and timeouts in EU inference endpoints. Traffic has been diverted away from the affected availability zone while we investigate. No data loss. Engineers are working on a remediation and ETA will be provided within 30 minutes."

sam_product: thanks. Please include the temporary workaround (routing diversion) in the update.

leo_runtime: monitoring: p99 latency for inference-service-rrg across prod now trending down from 2.3s -> 520ms, error-rate dropping to 0.8%. Good signal.

mike_infra: cordon/drain completed for 6 nodes. Autoscaler new config applied to exclude az1a for 1h.

ben_oncall: I'm taking the incident for the next shift. handoff notes: root cause suspected NIC offload regression after kernel update. Actions taken: routing diversion, cordon/drain, autoscaler exclusion, customer notifications. Next steps: rollback kernel on a canary node in az1a and test, or engage NIC vendor if flaky.

tanya_sre: agreed. ben, please coordinate rollback canary and share test results. I'll update the incident record and severity to Sev2 (service degradation impacting subset of customers).

maria_support: updating tickets and adding credit/communication placeholders.

status-bot: Incident update posted to status page: https://status.example/incidents/INF-2026-009.

ben_oncall: taking over. ping me for anything urgent. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INF-2026-009 created, Sev2, owner: ben_oncall, start_ts: 1759876543.

leo_runtime: note for postmortem: add tracing for TCP retransmit rate per-request, and consider making routing sensitive to node-level tx_hang metrics to automate early diversion.

mike_infra: I'll capture node logs and bundle NIC telemetry to attach to the postmortem.

sam_product: thanks team. keep me posted on rollback test outcome.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next update expected by 1759876900 (15 min).
